clue.text: Dad (about 50) shows signs of age, circumventing loud mates

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the word for dad is wrapped around the numeral

parts.note: dad is PA
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: circumventing means going round, so the ageing word surrounds the musical letter

parts.note: paper that yellows is showing its age
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: An old father, about fifty, is showing his age while avoiding his noisy friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'circumventing' both mean going round; paper yellows as it ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Playfellows are companions in games, a synonym for friends or pals.

clue.text: One standing in body of water to smell bad with two hours gone

indicators.note: gone says the two named letters disappear from the combined words

parts.note: a loch is a Scottish lake
to hum is slang for to stink
H is the abbreviation for hour, so two of them are HH

explanation.surface: A picture of someone standing in a stinking lake for two hours.
explanation.walkthrough: LOCH plus HUM gives LOCHHUM; taking out both H's leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric who deputises, someone substituting temporarily.

clue.text: Two unknowns penning article on great European river

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen holds sheep, so the two letters surround the middle part

parts.note: Y and Z are algebra's unknowns
an is the indefinite article
GT is the abbreviation for great

explanation.surface: Two strangers write an article about a famous river of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great European river' looks like the definition, but the Yangtze is Chinese: 'great' and 'European' are wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia, flowing across China.

clue.text: Crude yard at the back of where we live

indicators.note: at the back of puts the abbreviation after the planet's name

parts.note: we live on the planet Earth

explanation.surface: A rough backyard behind the house where we live.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse or bawdy, a synonym for crude.

clue.text: Dean's shown up without pill I drop to get wasted

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the drug letter is removed
in a down clue, shown up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a dean or dene is a valley, so a vale
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet
to shed is to drop, as leaves are shed

explanation.surface: A man called Dean appears without a pill that someone drops in order to get high.
explanation.walkthrough: VALE reversed is ELAV; without E it is LAV. The 's of Dean's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Money lavished on something is spent extravagantly, squandered.

clue.text: Land with craft, repressing resistance to row

indicators.note: repressing means holding down inside, so the physics letter sits within the word

parts.note: to wangle is to obtain by craftiness
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone lands a boat while trying to hold back resistance to rowing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrangle is a long noisy argument, a row in the quarrel sense.

clue.text: Having no leader, manage sensibly with respect to employment

indicators.note: having no leader means the phrase loses its first letter

parts.note: to cope is to manage
rationally means sensibly

explanation.surface: A leaderless group must manage its staff sensibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Operationally means in terms of how something is used or operates, its use in practice.

clue.text: Feed the desire of Empress of Blandings, maybe

indicators.note: of links owner and thing owned, putting the possessor's name first

parts.note: the Empress of Blandings is P. G. Wodehouse's prize pig, so an example of a pig; read as possessive
will means desire or wish

explanation.surface: A question of feeding Wodehouse's famous sow as she wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Empress of Blandings is Lord Emsworth's champion pig in P. G. Wodehouse's Blandings novels; the pig's will is what she wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigswill is kitchen waste fed to pigs, a kind of animal food.

clue.text: Large comic has cracks for those that defend veggies

indicators.note: cracks means breaks up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A big comedian makes jokes on behalf of vegetarians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'veggies' suggests vegetarians, but here it means vegetable crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrochemicals such as pesticides protect crops, including vegetables, from pests.

clue.text: Tree about to be planted in enclosure

indicators.note: planted in means set inside, so the short word goes within the enclosure

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
CA is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A tree is about to be planted in a fenced area.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is a hickory tree of North America grown for its nuts.

clue.text: Old sportsman inside at no time turned good to be telltale

indicators.note: inside puts the boxer's name within the turned word
turned means written back to front

parts.note: never means at no time
Muhammad Ali, the retired boxer

explanation.surface: A retired athlete who never went to the bad gives himself away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives REVEN from NEVER; the old sportsman is Muhammad Ali, the retired boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale sign is one that gives something away, disclosing it.

clue.text: Cheers let out about revolutionary headwear for further games

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the turned hat
let out suggests the letters are freed and loosened into a new order
revolutionary means turning over, so the hat word is reversed

parts.note: a tam is a Scottish bonnet, a tam-o'-shanter

explanation.surface: A cheer goes up around a revolutionary's cap at the next round of matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let out' turns Cheers into RECHES, which goes 'about' the revolutionary tam: a tam is a Scottish bonnet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rematches are repeat contests played again between the same sides.

clue.text: Ring to pull back covering opening of sandwich relish

indicators.note: covering means wrapped around, so the reversed letters enclose the initial
pull back read as turning the pair backwards

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
to tug is to pull

indicators.note: opening of takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Pulling back a ring-pull to open a sandwich spread.
explanation.walkthrough: O plus TUG reversed gives GUTO, which goes round S.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is enthusiasm or zest, as in eating with relish.

clue.text: What could be shocking about temperature sample

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the stun gun goes round the letter

parts.note: a Taser is an electric stun gun that gives a shock

explanation.surface: A shocking example of temperature readings.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small portion offered to try, a sample.

clue.text: Basic roofing material's brilliance keeping one beneath dry

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the shine contains the other letters

parts.note: sheen means lustre or brilliance

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath puts the numeral below, so after the dry letters

parts.note: TT is teetotal, so dry
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cheap roof's shine keeps a person dry underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheet tin, corrugated metal sheeting, is a cheap and simple covering for a shed or hut roof.

clue.text: Extremely excited swimmer, hugging constantly

indicators.note: hugging means holding tight round, so the swimmer encloses the adverb

parts.note: a fish is a swimmer
ever means always or constantly

explanation.surface: A thrilled swimmer is always embracing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish activity is frantic and agitated, intensely worked up.

clue.text: Retort back about parking on junction, with repeated directions

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for back goes round the parking letter

parts.note: rear means back
P is the sign for parking
a T is a junction shaped like the letter

indicators.note: repeated means the compass letter appears twice

parts.note: E for east is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A sharp reply about parking at a T-junction, with directions given twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick witty reply and banter, the exchange of comebacks.

clue.text: Went above water pipe with end of rake to push out second duck

indicators.note: to push out second says the new letter drives out the later of the two round letters

parts.note: an overflow is a pipe draining excess water
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, shaped like O

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A water pipe and a rake used to drive off a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: OVERFLOW has two O's; the second becomes E. A duck is a nought, cricket's score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Overflew is the past tense of overfly, to fly over a place.

clue.text: Hold back ball in panic

indicators.note: in places the sphere within the word for dread

parts.note: fear is panic or dread
an orb is a ball or sphere

explanation.surface: Someone holds back a ball in a moment of panic.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to refrain or restrain oneself from doing something.

clue.text: Fastidious about the Spanish exam

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fussy word goes round the article

parts.note: prim means prissy, fastidious
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A fussy teacher frets about a Spanish exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelim is a preliminary examination, such as a first-year university test.

clue.text: One present often overturned to carry, held by parent

indicators.note: held by means contained within, so the verb for raising children goes round

parts.note: to parent is to rear a child

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to lug is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: A frequent visitor's gift is overturned when a parent tries to carry it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parent' is a verb here, to bring up a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a habitual customer or frequent attender, someone always there.

clue.text: Writer's block finally disappearing

indicators.note: finally disappearing means the last letter vanishes

parts.note: a barrier is a block or obstruction

explanation.surface: Writer's block finally lifts.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says writer's block, but the 's is 'is' joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie was the Scottish author of Peter Pan.

clue.text: Chop off head of beam to make post

indicators.note: chop off head of means remove the first letter

parts.note: a rafter is a roof beam

explanation.surface: Chopping the end off a beam to make a fence post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like timber, but it is post- meaning later, as in postwar.
explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix, post- means later than, as in postwar or postscript.

clue.text: Glance as criminal hides one drug

indicators.note: hides means conceals within, so the shuffled letters hold the numeral
criminal suggests wrong, crooked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A glance at a criminal who is hiding a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: An analgesic is a painkiller, a medicine such as aspirin.

clue.text: Go on without interruption, crucial to amuse guest

indicators.note: crucial to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Carrying on without a break is vital to keeping a guest entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: To segue is to move smoothly into the next item, continuing seamlessly.

clue.text: City in France that's east of island, beset by westerly wind

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the reversed word goes round the rest
in an across clue, westerly means read right to left

parts.note: to reel is to wind, as a fishing line

indicators.note: east of in an across clue means placed to the right, so after

parts.note: c'est is French for that is

explanation.surface: A French city to the east of an island, battered by a westerly gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City in France' looks like the definition, but Leicester is English; 'in France that's' gives C'EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a city in the English East Midlands.

clue.text: Allowed a labrador initially to get on part of sofa

indicators.note: to get on means climb onto, so the dog letters come after the furniture part

parts.note: a sofa stands on legs

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A labrador is permitted to climb onto the sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal means permitted by law, lawful.

clue.text: Preserved complimentary final letter by king that's died

parts.note: complimentary means given free of charge
zed is the last letter of the alphabet
R is rex, Latin for king
ie is id est, Latin for that is
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A free last letter written by a king who has since died, kept for posterity.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is freeze-dried is preserved by rapid freezing and dehydration.
